BOTH its power inputs are on the front - an IEC C14 inlet and a -48 to -60 V pluggable DC terminal - and the rear carries only two fixed fans.","format":1,"gaps":[{"reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["front"],"wanted":"THE AC RATING PRINTED UNDER THE INLET. The silkscreen is modelled as the figure prints it and the attr as the specification states it; a photograph of a real unit's legend settles which is printed.","what":"ac-rating-silkscreen"},{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["front"],"wanted":"WHETHER THE MGMT JACK HAS LAMPS. One document, stated once, shared with the non-I 28Fv2."},"figure-choice":{"confidence":"measured","note":"Gate 1. THE GUIDE DRAWS THIS VARIANT BY NAME: embedded image q-004, 1811 x 220, whose name bar reads ECS4120-28Fv2-I (its sibling q-002 reads ECS4120-28Fv2). The face is drawn front-on under a lid shown in perspective; it spans x 0-1806 and y 47-217 below the lid seam. 1807 px across 440 mm is 4.107 px/mm. THE BOX IS NOT SQUARE, SO THE FEATURES DECIDE. 171 px of face height would be 41.6 mm at that scale against the stated 44. Two standard features were read on both axes: the MGMT and Console bezels measure 15.83 mm across against the RJ-45 housing's 15.8, and the two ports of an SFP stack sit 64 px apart - 15.55 mm isotropically, 3.7% over the registry's 15.0 belly-to-belly pitch, where the box's own vertical scale would make it 16.5, 10% over. So the drawing is read isotropically at 4.107 px/mm and anchored on its bottom edge (y 217 = 44.0 mm); the top 2.7 mm under the lid seam is the chamfer the lid is drawn over. Vertical positions are the least certain numbers here, to about 1.5 mm. THE CAGES KEEP THE REGISTRY'S GEOMETRY and the lamps are placed to clear it. A two-high stack of std/sfp-ganged openings, 10.4 tall on the registry's 15.0 row pitch, spans 25.4 mm where the drawn frame spans 24.4 - the drawing is squashed vertically, as the box said. So the stacks run y 13.0-38.4 and the lamps sit 0.2 mm clear under them at 39.6, about 0.35 mm lower than drawn, rather than overlapping the cage they serve. ORTHOGRAPHIC: the twelve stacks' lamp pairs fit a straight line to 0.21 px on a 71.48 px (17.405 mm) pitch."},"lamps":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"One white oval lamp per port under every SFP and RJ-45 stack, a pair 5.97 mm apart, each over its own legend - so each is assigned to the port its legend names. The SFP+ ports' lamps are not under them: they sit in a 3 x 2 block to the left of MGMT with DIAG and PWR, legended '25 27 DIAG' above and '26 28 PWR' below. The guide's 'On/Blinking Green - Port has a valid link' is the only lamp semantics given, and its 'PWR and DIAG' are the -I's system lamps."},"left-end":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"BOTH INPUTS ARE ON THE FRONT, as the drawing and all three photographs show, though the guide's generic text says 'the AC input socket on the back of the switch' - that sentence covers the 28T and 52T it shares the page with. An IEC C14 inlet in a recess at x 4.1-36.0; a ground stud with its symbol at x 47; and a green two-pole pluggable DC terminal at [64.8, 17.5], 32.6 x 18.0 - which is common/dc-terminal-plug-2@1 from the ECS4530-54CSFP-DC-I to within 0.5 mm (32.1 x 17.6), so the part is reused rather than drawn again. Its poles are printed '+' left and '-' right with '(DC)-48~-60V;3.0A' between - the opposite order to the ECS4530-DC-I's, which is a faceplate fact and not the part's."},"ports-and-numbering":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"READ OFF THE FACEPLATE. Twelve two-high SFP stacks, each legended 'n (up) n+1 (down)' beneath its two lamps: the top cage is the odd port and the bottom the even, 1-24. Two two-high RJ-45 stacks legended 21/22 and 23/24, and four single SFP+ cages under a '10G' bracket legended 25-28. The guide's transceiver list is 1000BASE optics (ET4202-*) and 10GBASE optics (ET5402-*), which is the 1G/10G split. THE COMBO PAIRING IS THE FACEPLATE'S, NOT THE GUIDE'S. The same numbers 21-24 are printed under the eleventh and twelfth SFP stacks AND under the two RJ-45 stacks, which is how this vendor marks combo ports. Neither the converted text nor the PDF's own text layer contains 'combo', 'shared' or 'either' - two searches - so this rests on the legend alone and is recorded as such; the copper jacks are named copper-21..24 and their group says what they share."},"rear":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"THE WEAKEST NUMBERS HERE. No figure draws this model's rear; the only evidence is the 489 px rear product photograph at about 1.08 px/mm. It shows two fixed fans behind honeycomb guards centred at 109.8 and 236.1 mm, each about 51.7 x 26.9, from y 5.4 - to a millimetre and a half at best. No handles or seams: fixed fans, drawn as the panel's perforation. The guide contains no 'fan' at all, in its converted text or its PDF text layer."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"ONE DOCUMENT, AND NO DATASHEET WAS EVER PUBLISHED - the product page carries the quick start guide, safety notes and firmware only. ecs4120-28fv2-i-qsg is the ECS4120 Series guide, nine pages, trilingual (English, simplified and traditional Chinese) and covering four models (28T, 52T, 28Fv2, 28Fv2-I). Its 72 embedded images reduce to 19 unique ones of useful size once the three languages' repeats are removed by content hash, so no figure is counted as more than one piece of evidence. Three 489 px product photographs of this model are staged. ISSUE #343 SAID THE CHASSIS IS 'NOT STATED IN ANY STAGED DOCUMENT', AND IT IS STATED. The guide's Hardware Specifications table gives '28Fv2/28Fv2-I: 44.0 x 22.0 x 4.4 cm (17.32 x 8.66 x 1.73 in)', '2.82 kg (6.22 lb)', the -I's own operating range, its AC and DC input ratings and its 60 W maximum - enough for the whole attrs block below."},"stack-orientation":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 12 SFP pairs (port-1/port-2 to port-23/port-24). 12 of these were drawn with the upper cage turned before the std cage art moved its lip to the bottom of the opening; turning them keeps the lips in the middle band where they were drawn and seats every optic bail-outward."},"vents":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"A row of 54 vertical slots across the top of the port field, x 103.7-370.6, 2.43 mm wide on a 4.99 mm pitch, running from the lid seam down to about 8.8 mm."}},"references":[{"sha256":"5e6be7749223fe5ea8b133614b15dc1598a6fde06f5792df041896e7f1c1adf9","title":"Edgecore ECS4120 Series 28-Port and 52-Port L2 Gigabit Ethernet Switches
